changed.title: One shared set of parity checks recovers the hidden payload on both sides of a cyclic intersection encoding
changed.statement:
∀ (a b h s q : Nat) (hn : 0 < a+b), 0 < q → 0 < s → s ≤ h →
  q*h < a → (q+1)*h ≤ b →
  let n := a+b
  let M := q^2 * (2^s-1)^(2*(q-1)) * 2^(n-(2*q*s+(h-s)))
  let Word := Fin n → Bool
  let Pat := Fin (n-h) → Bool
  let Slot := Fin n × Pat
  let loc := fun k : Nat => (⟨k%n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩ : Fin n)
  let solutions := fun (tab : Slot → Bool) =>
    (Finset.univ : Finset Word).filter (fun x =>
      ∀ i : Fin n, tab (i,fun j => x (loc (i.val+j.val))) = true)
  ∃ (code : Fin M → Word) (base : Slot → Bool) (left right : Fin M → Slot),
    Function.Injective code ∧ Function.Injective left ∧ Function.Injective right ∧
    (∀ i, (left i).1.val < a ∧ a ≤ (right i).1.val ∧
      base (left i) = false ∧ base (right i) = false) ∧
    ∀ A B : Finset (Fin M), solutions (fun slot =>
      base slot || decide (slot ∈ A.image left) || decide (slot ∈ B.image right)) =
        (A ∩ B).image code
changed.unlocks: encodes two mask inputs on a cyclic table with a common collection of parity checks
changed.context: Give each tile s label bits. Require exactly one zero label per arc. Across all tiles require even parity in each of the h-s other columns. One guard sees every tile because the final h sites are reserved. Arc guards see their full arcs. Put each word's port just after its marked tile. Its window misses only that tile. The mark fixes its label and the shared checks recover its other bits. Count the marked sites, nonzero labels and free payload coordinates. A guarded word passes exactly its two switches.

changed.title: The sole binary-formula density strictly between seven sixteenths and one half has a unique five-variable form
changed.statement:
∀ n : ℕ,
  let W := Fin n → Bool
  let Lit := Fin n × Bool
  let F := Finset (Lit × Lit)
  let sat := fun (C : F) (w : W) => decide (∀ c ∈ C,
    w c.1.1 ≠ c.1.2 ∨ w c.2.1 ≠ c.2.2)
  let Q := 2 ^ n
  ∀ A : F,
    let N := (Finset.univ.filter (fun z => sat A z = true)).card
    let cert := ∀ x : W, sat A x = true →
      ∃ T : Finset (Fin n), T.card ≤ 2 ∧
        ∀ y : W, (∀ i ∈ T, y i = x i) → sat A y = true
    let half := ∃ (j : Fin n) (v : Bool), ∀ p : W, p j = v → sat A p = true
    let shape := ∃ (sites : Fin 5 → Fin n) (signs : Fin 5 → Bool),
      Function.Injective sites ∧ ∀ word : W,
        let mark := fun k : Fin 5 => word (sites k) = signs k
        sat A word = decide (¬(mark 0 ∧ (mark 1 ∨ mark 2)) ∧ ¬(mark 3 ∧ mark 4))
    (Q ≤ 2 * N → half ∨ cert) ∧ (2 * N = Q → cert) ∧
      ((7 * Q < 16 * N ∧ 2 * N < Q) ↔ shape) ∧
      (shape → 32 * N = 15 * Q)
changed.unlocks: identifies the only hidden binary-clause density strictly between seven sixteenths and one half and classifies its predicates
changed.context: Unary exclusions and conflicting forbidden pairs give half cores with certificates of size two. Otherwise orient every bit consistently and count independent sets. With matching number at most one get a star or triangle. Beside two matched edges, a third gives three disjoint edges (27/64), a four-vertex path (1/2), or a two-edge path and separate edge (15/32). Every passing word of the four-vertex path has a two-bit certificate, and the last graph has three-bit certificates. Any further clause cutting a core loses at least 1/16 or 1/32 respectively.

changed.title: Cyclic runs count the input masks with nonzero Walsh coefficient and bound the loss under a singular three-tap mix
changed.statement:
∀ (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] (d : ℕ),
  let I := ZMod k
  let B := ZMod 2
  let V := I → B
  let sign := fun (t : B) => if t = 0 then (1 : ℤ) else -1
  let mix := fun (s : ℕ) (x : V) (i : I) => x (i-(s : I)) + x i + x (i+(s : I))
  let nl := fun (y : V) (j : I) => y j + (1+y (j+1))*y (j+2)
  let coeff := fun (s : ℕ) (a b : V) =>
    ∑ x : V, sign (dotProduct a x + dotProduct b (nl (mix s x)))
  let support := fun (s : ℕ) (b : V) => Finset.univ.filter (fun mask : V => coeff s mask b ≠ 0)
  let g := Nat.gcd k d
  let h := if 3 ∣ k/g then 2*g else 0
  ∀ b : V,
    let edge := fun (w : V) (i : I) => b (i-2)*w (i-1) + b (i-1)*w (i+1)
    let run := fun (i : I) =>
      ((List.range k).takeWhile (fun offset => decide (b (i+(offset : I)) = 1))).length
    let r := if ∀ i : I, b i = 1 then k - Nat.gcd k 2 else
      ∑ i : I, if b i = 1 ∧ b (i-1) = 0 then 2*((run i + 1)/2) else 0
    (∃ base : V, ∀ a : V, a ∈ support d b ↔
      ∃ u : V, a = base + mix d (edge (mix d u))) ∧
    (support 0 b).card = 2^r ∧
    (support d b).card ≤ 2^r ∧ 2^r ≤ 2^(2*h) * (support d b).card
changed.unlocks: An affine basis enumerates the contributing predecessors of a requested output mask in the shared-key transfer. Summing the run weights prices a full layer.
changed.context: Polarize the mask polynomial. Its matrix after mixing is M E M, where E is the selected cycle adjacency in the term. On the radical, q(x)+q(0) is linear. Extend it to a frequency. The other extensions differ by the polar image, and the checked quadratic Walsh formula detects exactly these. A proper run gives a path on l+1 vertices: the endpoint forces alternate kernel entries zero, leaving one free only for odd order. The full cycle kernel is two-periodic. Each multiplication by M drops rank by at most its nullity h; on a spacing orbit its kernel repeats A,B,A+B.

changed.title: A two-state trace counts all nonzero Walsh transitions of the unmixed cyclic row and bounds both scheduled spacings at every width
changed.statement:
∀ (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] (d : ℕ),
  let I := ZMod k
  let B := ZMod 2
  let V := I → B
  let sign := fun (t : B) => if t = 0 then (1 : ℤ) else -1
  let mix := fun (s : ℕ) (x : V) (i : I) => x (i-(s : I)) + x i + x (i+(s : I))
  let nl := fun (y : V) (j : I) => y j + (1+y (j+1))*y (j+2)
  let pairs := fun (s : ℕ) => ∑ b : V,
    (Finset.univ.filter (fun a : V =>
      (∑ x : V, sign (dotProduct a x + dotProduct b (nl (mix s x)))) ≠ 0)).card
  let A : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℤ := fun src dst =>
    if src = 0 then (if dst = 0 then 1 else 4) else (if dst = 0 then 2 else 0)
  let total := Matrix.trace (A^k) +
    (if k % 2 = 1 then (2:ℤ)^(k-1) else -7*(2:ℤ)^(k-2))
  let g := Nat.gcd k d
  let h := if 3 ∣ k/g then 2*g else 0
  (pairs 0 : ℤ) = total ∧ (pairs d : ℤ) ≤ total ∧
    total ≤ (2:ℤ)^(2*h) * (pairs d : ℤ) ∧ (2:ℤ)^k * total ≤ 3*(7:ℤ)^k
changed.unlocks: Counts candidate products across each full shared-key transfer layer, including singular widths, and identifies the exponential cost of enumerating these products.
changed.context: In a cyclic mask with a zero, that zero resets the parity of the current run to even. A one switches parity, with weight four out of even and one out of odd. Any zero has weight one. The trace sums these walks, uniquely for each proper mask. On all ones it counts zero for odd k and twice 2^k for even k. Replace that contribution by 2^(k-gcd(k,2)). Sum the column bounds to allow singular mixing. Cayley-Hamilton gives T(k+2)=T(k+1)+8T(k), with T(0)=2 and T(1)=1. Induction gives T(k) ≤ 2*(7/2)^k and the odd correction fits one more (7/2)^k.

Sum the column bounds to allow singular mixing. Cayley-Hamilton gives T(k+2)=T(k+1)+8T(k), with T(0)=2 and T(1)=1. Induction gives T(k) ≤ 2*(7/2)^k and the odd correction fits one more (7/2)^k.

changed.title: A matching of a coordinate selector attains a logarithmic improvement below one-quarter error with only paired OR signals
changed.statement:
∀ (k a c : ℕ), 2 ≤ a → 2^a ≤ k → c < a →
  let N := 2^k
  let r := 2^a
  let b := 2^c
  let m := 2^(a-1-c)
  let Z := 2^(r/2)
  let hit := Z - (2^b-2)^m
  let base := fun (x y : Fin N) => x.val.testBit (y.val % r)
  ∃ (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin N)) (flip : Fin N → Bool),
    let errors := fun (G : Fin N → Fin N → Bool) (decode : Finset (Fin N) → Bool) =>
      (Finset.univ.filter (fun z : Fin N × Fin N =>
        decode ({z.1,z.2} : Finset (Fin N)) ≠ xor (G z.1 (π z.2)) (flip z.1))).card
    let cost := errors base
    ∃ best : Finset (Fin N) → Bool,
      (∀ other : Finset (Fin N) → Bool, cost best ≤ cost other) ∧
      8*r*Z^2*cost best + b*N^2*hit^2 = 2*r*Z^2*N^2 ∧
      (2*b ≤ a → a < 4*b → 128*r*cost best + a*N^2 ≤ 32*r*N^2) ∧
      ∀ (A B : Finset (Fin N)) (T : Fin N → Fin N → Bool),
        (∀ x ∉ A, ∀ y ∉ B, T x y = base x y) →
        errors T best + (N-A.card)*(N-B.card) ≤ cost best + N^2
changed.unlocks: Determines the order of the finite gap below one-quarter error when the selector matching is optimized, by pairing this construction with the all-matching moment floor.
changed.context: Split r/2 active bits into b-bit blocks. Inactive bits give a bank, start and offset. In bank zero take the first constant block cyclically or the start on failure. Switch by its common bit on success and zero otherwise. In bank one select a uniform inactive label and switch by the XOR of two active bits. Each group has N/r rows. The signed matrix has zero inactive rows and active entries (N/r)H/Z inside blocks, zero between blocks. The trace of its square counts swap agreements minus disagreements. Each discordant unordered pair costs one error.

The signed matrix has zero inactive rows and active entries (N/r)H/Z inside blocks, zero between blocks. The trace of its square counts swap agreements minus disagreements. Each discordant unordered pair costs one error.
